learn.rule: Because gives the reason. But shows a contrast or surprise. So shows the result.
learn.ruleEs: Because da la razón. But muestra un contraste o una sorpresa. So muestra el resultado.
learn.model: Engineers in Tokyo design flexible skyscrapers because earthquakes are common in Japan.
learn.notice: Look at what comes after because: it explains why. Then try the same stem with but and so.

items.prompt: Which ending completes the earthquake sentence with because?
items.text: Engineers in Tokyo design flexible skyscrapers because ___

options.text: so fewer buildings are damaged.
earthquakes are common in Japan.
but some older buildings stay rigid.

items.why: Because is followed by the reason. Earthquakes are common explains why engineers build flexible towers.
items.whyEs: Because va seguido de la razón. Earthquakes are common explica por qué los ingenieros hacen torres flexibles.

items.prompt: Which ending shows a result of the tremor, using so?
items.text: Seismometers detected a strong tremor near the coast, so ___

options.text: because the plates had shifted underground.
but the water stayed calm.
the tsunami warning was sent within minutes.

items.why: So introduces what happened because of the first part. The warning was a result of detecting the tremor.
items.whyEs: So presenta lo que pasó a causa de la primera parte. La alerta fue el resultado de detectar el temblor.

items.prompt: Choose the connector that fits the meaning.
items.model: The ground shook violently, but the reinforced buildings stood firm.
items.why: The two parts are a surprise together: strong shaking, yet the buildings held. That contrast calls for but.
items.whyEs: Las dos partes forman una sorpresa: sacudida fuerte, pero los edificios resistieron. Ese contraste pide but.

items.prompt: Fill both blanks to explain the work of fault-line scientists.
parts: they want to predict where earthquakes will happen,
no one can predict the exact day.
items.model: Scientists study fault lines because they want to predict where earthquakes will happen, but no one can predict the exact day.
items.why: The first blank gives a reason (because they want to predict). The second shows a contrast with what scientists still cannot do (but).
items.whyEs: El primer espacio da una razón (because they want to predict). El segundo muestra un contraste con lo que aún no pueden hacer (but).

items.prompt: Check every ending about the fault that fits the word but.
items.text: Many people live near the San Andreas Fault, but ___

options.text: scientists warn that a major quake could strike someday.
so they keep emergency kits at home.
some residents choose to move inland.
because the land is affordable.
that is why the fault is closely studied.

items.why: But signals something different or unexpected. So and because give a result or a reason, and the last choice does not contrast at all.
items.whyEs: But señala algo diferente o inesperado. So y because dan un resultado o una razón, y la última opción no contrasta nada.

items.prompt: Which sentence uses so to show a result correctly?

options.text: The building swayed without breaking, so it was built with flexible steel.
The building was built with flexible steel, so it swayed without breaking.
The building was built with flexible steel, so because it swayed without breaking.

items.why: The steel comes first and the swaying without breaking is the result. Check the order: cause first, then so, then the result.
items.whyEs: El acero va primero y balancearse sin romperse es el resultado. Revisa el orden: causa, luego so, luego el resultado.

write.prompt: Finish the sentence three ways: with because, with but, and with so.
write.promptEs: Termina la oración de tres maneras: con because, con but y con so.
write.text: Cities in earthquake zones adopt strict building codes
write.frame: Cities in earthquake zones adopt strict building codes ___

label: I used because to give a reason
Usé because para dar una razón
I used but to show a contrast
Usé but para mostrar un contraste
I used so to show a result
Usé so para mostrar un resultado

write.model: Cities in earthquake zones adopt strict building codes because buildings must survive strong shaking. Cities in earthquake zones adopt strict building codes, but older buildings may still need repairs. Cities in earthquake zones adopt strict building codes, so new towers are safer.

familyTalk.en: Pick a rule at home or school. Say it three ways: 'We have this rule because ... but ... so ...'
familyTalk.es: Elijan una regla de la casa o la escuela. Díganla de tres maneras: 'Tenemos esta regla because ... but ... so ...'

teacherTip.en: Have pairs say all three versions aloud before writing, and ask which connector changes the meaning most.
teacherTip.es: Pide que las parejas digan las tres versiones en voz alta antes de escribir, y pregunta qué conector cambia más el significado.

learn.rule: Because gives the reason. But shows a contrast or surprise. So shows the result.
learn.ruleEs: Because da la razón. But muestra un contraste o una sorpresa. So muestra el resultado.
learn.model: Factories multiplied in northern England because coal and iron were close by.
learn.notice: Each connector changes what the second part means: reason, contrast, or result.

items.prompt: Which ending completes the Industrial Revolution sentence with because?
items.text: Factories multiplied in northern England because ___

options.text: coal and iron were close by.
so cities grew rapidly.
but wages stayed low.

items.why: Coal and iron were close by explains why factories spread there. Because always points to the reason.
items.whyEs: Coal and iron were close by explica por qué las fábricas se extendieron ahí. Because siempre apunta a la razón.

items.prompt: Which ending shows the result of faster spinning, using so?
items.text: Machines could spin thread much faster than workers by hand, so ___

options.text: because owners wanted lower costs.
cloth became cheaper and easier to buy.
but many weavers lost their work.

items.why: Cheaper cloth is what happened as a result of faster spinning. So connects the cause to its effect.
items.whyEs: La tela más barata es lo que pasó como resultado de hilar más rápido. So une la causa con su efecto.

items.prompt: Choose the connector that shows the result.
parts: merchants could sell to distant towns.
items.model: Railroads carried goods quickly, so merchants could sell to distant towns.
items.why: Fast shipping led to selling in far towns. That is cause then result, so the connector is so.
items.whyEs: El transporte rápido llevó a vender en pueblos lejanos. Es causa y luego resultado, así que el conector es so.

items.prompt: Fill both blanks to explain why families moved to cities.
parts: the work was often long and dangerous.
items.model: Many families moved to cities because factories offered steady wages, but the work was often long and dangerous.
items.why: The first blank gives the reason families moved (because wages). The second shows a downside that surprises us (but the work was dangerous).
items.whyEs: El primer espacio da la razón de la mudanza (because wages). El segundo muestra un lado negativo inesperado (but the work was dangerous).

items.prompt: Check every ending about child labor that fits the word but.
items.text: Child labor helped factories run cheaply, but ___

options.text: reformers argued that children belonged in school.
so Parliament passed laws limiting hours.
the long hours harmed children's health.
because families needed the extra income.

items.why: But introduces an idea that pushes against the first part. So gives a result and because gives a reason, so those do not fit.
items.whyEs: But introduce una idea que se opone a la primera parte. So da un resultado y because una razón, así que no encajan.

options.text: Cities grew crowded, so sanitation became a serious problem.
Cities grew crowded, but many workers still preferred them to farms.
Cities grew crowded because so many workers moved there for jobs.

items.why: Because explains why cities grew crowded: workers moved there for jobs. The other two sentences show a result and a contrast.
items.whyEs: Because explica por qué las ciudades se llenaron: los trabajadores llegaron por empleo. Las otras dos muestran un resultado y un contraste.

write.prompt: Finish the sentence three ways: with because, with but, and with so.
write.promptEs: Termina la oración de tres maneras: con because, con but y con so.
write.text: The Industrial Revolution changed daily life
write.frame: The Industrial Revolution changed daily life ___

label: I used because to give a reason
Usé because para dar una razón
I used but to show a contrast
Usé but para mostrar un contraste
I used so to show a result
Usé so para mostrar un resultado

write.model: The Industrial Revolution changed daily life because machines replaced much hand work. The Industrial Revolution changed daily life, but many workers faced harsh conditions. The Industrial Revolution changed daily life, so more people moved to cities.

familyTalk.en: Talk about a change in your family's life, such as a new phone or a move. Use because, but, and so to describe it.
familyTalk.es: Hablen de un cambio en la vida de su familia, como un teléfono nuevo o una mudanza. Usen because, but y so para describirlo.

teacherTip.en: Ask students to find a real cause, a real contrast, and a real effect in the unit before they write their three sentences.
teacherTip.es: Pide que busquen en la unidad una causa real, un contraste real y un efecto real antes de escribir sus tres oraciones.

learn.rule: Because gives the reason. But shows a contrast or surprise. So shows the result.
learn.ruleEs: Because da la razón. But muestra un contraste o una sorpresa. So muestra el resultado.
learn.model: The larger cereal box is the better buy because its price per ounce is lower.
learn.notice: In math writing, because explains a reason, but marks a surprise, and so announces a conclusion.

items.prompt: Which ending completes the cereal sentence with because?
items.text: The larger cereal box is the better buy because ___

options.text: so it costs more in total.
but the smaller box is easier to carry.
its price per ounce is lower.

items.why: A lower price per ounce is the reason the larger box is the better buy. Because leads to the reason.
items.whyEs: Un precio menor por onza es la razón por la que la caja grande conviene más. Because lleva a la razón.

items.prompt: Which ending shows the result of comparing unit prices, using so?
items.text: Brand B costs $0.12 per ounce and Brand A costs $0.15 per ounce, so ___

options.text: because Mia wanted the cheaper brand.
Mia chose Brand B to save money.
but Brand A has a bigger label.

items.why: Comparing the unit prices led to Mia's choice. The second part is the result of the first part.
items.whyEs: Comparar los precios por unidad llevó a la decisión de Mia. La segunda parte es el resultado de la primera.

items.prompt: Choose the connector that completes the ratio sentence.
parts: The ratio of boys to girls in the club is 3 to 2,
a club of 25 students has 15 boys and 10 girls.
items.model: The ratio of boys to girls in the club is 3 to 2, so a club of 25 students has 15 boys and 10 girls.
items.why: Knowing the ratio lets us conclude how many students are in each group. A conclusion in math often begins with so.
items.whyEs: Conocer la razón nos permite concluir cuántos estudiantes hay en cada grupo. En matemáticas, una conclusión suele empezar con so.

items.prompt: Fill both blanks about unit rates.
parts: they make different deals easy to compare,
you must check that the units match.
items.model: Unit rates are useful because they make different deals easy to compare, but you must check that the units match.
items.why: The first blank gives the reason unit rates help (because). The second adds a warning that pushes against the idea (but).
items.whyEs: El primer espacio da la razón de su utilidad (because). El segundo agrega una advertencia que se opone a la idea (but).

items.prompt: Check every ending about the 12-ounce box that fits the word but.
items.text: The 12-ounce box costs less than the 20-ounce box, but ___

options.text: its unit price is higher.
so many shoppers choose it.
it holds fewer ounces for the money.
because the price tag is smaller.

items.why: But signals a surprise: the box costs less, yet it is not the better deal. So and because would give a result or a reason instead.
items.whyEs: But señala una sorpresa: la caja cuesta menos, pero no es la mejor oferta. So y because darían un resultado o una razón.

items.prompt: Which ending shows a result in the recipe sentence?
items.text: The recipe uses a 2:3 ratio of flour to milk, so ___

options.text: because the batter must be thick enough.
but it also needs two eggs.
3 cups of flour need 4.5 cups of milk.

items.why: Keeping the 2:3 ratio gives a result: for 3 cups of flour you scale the milk to 4.5 cups. So leads to the effect.
items.whyEs: Mantener la razón 2:3 da un resultado: para 3 tazas de harina, la leche se ajusta a 4.5 tazas. So lleva al efecto.

write.prompt: Finish the sentence three ways: with because, with but, and with so.
write.promptEs: Termina la oración de tres maneras: con because, con but y con so.

Usé because para dar una razón
I used but to show a contrast

I used so to show a result

write.model: The large bottle costs more because it holds more juice. The large bottle costs more, but its unit price is lower. The large bottle costs more, so the family compared unit prices before buying.

familyTalk.en: At the store, compare two sizes of the same item. Say: 'The big one costs more, but ... so we ...'
familyTalk.es: En la tienda, comparen dos tamaños del mismo producto. Digan: 'El grande cuesta más, but ... so ...'

teacherTip.en: Have students show the unit-price calculation next to each sentence so the connector is backed by the math.
teacherTip.es: Pide que muestren el cálculo del precio por unidad junto a cada oración para que el conector tenga respaldo matemático.
